## Overview

RLMADJ02 is the reduced Down-syndrome-only companion requested in #409 D3. It asks whether wave-1 verbal memory (`basdig`), receptive vocabulary (`bpvs`) and verbal reasoning (`bassim`) distinguish subsequent BAS word-reading gain within the Byrne cohort's Down syndrome group. Wave-3 word reading is conditioned on wave-1 word reading and the three standardised wave-1 predictors are entered together. The complete-case frame contains 22 of the 24 children with Down syndrome.

_Adjusted associations only._ This historical cohort has no intervention, and restricting it to one group does not create a causal design. Each coefficient is a between-child conditional association: it describes children who differed at baseline, conditional on the other named skills and baseline word reading. It does not say what would happen if memory, vocabulary or reasoning were changed.

_Why this set is deliberately small._ The pooled parent model, `lrp-rlm-adj-001`, contains five skill predictors, age and the own baseline. Carrying that seven-slope specification into about 21 Down syndrome rows would leave the mutually adjusted posteriors largely determined by their priors. This companion pre-specifies three confirmed-ceiling measures and excludes age as an additional slope. Its estimates therefore are not age-adjusted; that narrower conditional question is the price of keeping the model estimable. The three selected instruments have confirmed denominators, and the extract lineage was reconciled on 2026-08-16. A fit stored before that decision must still be regenerated because its release contract correctly preserves the earlier fail-closed input snapshot.

## Model

For child $i$ with wave-1 word-reading logit $b_i$ and standardised wave-1 predictors $z_{k,i}$:

$$
y_i \sim \mathrm{BetaBinomial}(90,\ p_i,\ \kappa),
\qquad
\operatorname{logit}(p_i) = \alpha + \gamma_{\text{own}} b_i +
\beta_{\text{basdig}}z_{\text{basdig},i} +
\beta_{\text{bpvs}}z_{\text{bpvs},i} +
\beta_{\text{bassim}}z_{\text{bassim},i}.
$$

Here $y_i$ is wave-3 BAS word reading out of 90. The three mutually adjusted slopes have $\mathrm{Normal}(0, 0.3)$ priors and are reported per one-standard-deviation predictor difference on both the logit and expected-word scales. No group nuisance coefficient is fitted because every row belongs to the Down syndrome group. Baseline-only bivariate refits, slope-prior sensitivity refits at prior standard deviations 0.5 and 0.7, and an own-baseline-prior refit widening $\gamma_{\text{own}} \sim \mathrm{Normal}(1, 0.25)$ to SD 0.5 remain required companions. The Beta-Binomial concentration takes the dispersion-scale prior of the Byrne historical families, $1/\sqrt{\kappa} \sim \mathrm{HalfNormal}(0.25)$, so the near-Binomial limit is not excluded a priori (2026-08-22 adjusted-family review).
